item.text:
**Assessment**
Mixed, leaning positive. The clearest evidence for 6B.5 is in health and social protection: Jokowi’s government used registry data, redistribution rules, monitoring, and response teams to improve delivery. The main negatives are incomplete reach in remote areas, digital divides, and some patronage/favoritism in implementation.

**Claims**
- [Indonesia](https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2024-2025/country-profile/2024/indonesia) — World Health Organization, 2024. Claim: WHO credits Indonesia with 90% health coverage, lower out-of-pocket costs, improved access regardless of gender/age/disability, and more efficient, results-oriented, transparent resource management. IDs: 6B.5; also 6B.2, 6B.3.
- [Does Indonesia’s National Health Insurance Scheme mobile phone application, Mobile JKN, support health financing?](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240100893) — World Health Organization, 2024-12-06. Claim: Mobile JKN simplified registration and payments, improved informal-sector contribution collection, and lowered BPJS administrative costs. IDs: 6B.5; also 6B.2.
- [Does Indonesia’s National Health Insurance Scheme mobile phone application, Mobile JKN, support health financing?](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240100893) — World Health Organization, 2024-12-06. Claim: The same WHO review says digital literacy, smartphone ownership, internet connectivity, and interoperability gaps limited Mobile JKN’s full impact. IDs: 6B.5; also 6B.2.
- [Less burden, better care: MoH and WHO accelerate JKN redistribution](https://www.who.int/indonesia/news/detail/29-10-2024-less-burden--better-care--moh-and-who-accelerate-jkn-redistribution) — World Health Organization Indonesia, 2024-10-29. Claim: MoH, WHO, and stakeholders agreed to redistribute patients and resources across primary-care providers, using workload ratios, quality standards, and continuous monitoring/evaluation to balance service quality. IDs: 6B.5; also 6B.2.
- [BAPPENAS Perkuat Dukungan untuk Anak-Anak dan Keluarga Rentan](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/id/press-releases/bappenas-perkuat-dukungan-untuk-anak-anak-dan-keluarga-rentan) — UNICEF Indonesia, 2024-04-25. Claim: Regsosek was presented as a data system to improve targeting, delivery, accountability, and transparency of social assistance for poor and vulnerable households. IDs: 6B.5; also 6B.2, 6B.3.
- [Indonesia ramps up capacities to detect and respond to outbreaks of emerging and epidemic-prone diseases](https://www.who.int/indonesia/news-room/item/30-08-2024-indonesia-ramps-up-capacities-to-detect-and-respond-to-outbreaks-of-emerging-and-epidemic-prone-diseases) — World Health Organization Indonesia, 2024-08-30. Claim: The Ministry of Health and WHO trained rapid-response teams in 514 districts to do early detection, verification, field investigation, risk assessment, and outbreak response. IDs: 6B.5; also 6B.2.
- [Computation and Analysis of Macro Poverty of Indonesia 2024](https://www.bps.go.id/en/publication/2024/11/29/31e54c0717742a2dc13300e4/penghitungan-dan-analisis-kemiskinan-makro-di-indonesia-tahun-2024.htm) — BPS-Statistics Indonesia, 2024-11-29. Claim: Indonesia’s official poverty statistics are explicitly built for planning, monitoring, and evaluating poverty programs using March 2024 Susenas data, showing a measurement infrastructure available to the administration. IDs: 6B.5; also 6B.2.
- [Social Protection Inclusion in Indonesia’s Remote Areas - Identifying and Addressing Gaps and Challenges](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099062624071020814) — World Bank, 2024-06-01. Claim: Poor and vulnerable households in remote areas still faced barriers to accessing social protection, so the system improved in design but remained uneven in practice. IDs: 6B.5; also 6B.2, 6B.3.
- [World Bank Group debars PT LPPSLH Konsultan](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/10/world-bank-group-debars-pt-lppslh-konsultan) — World Bank, 2024-07-10. Claim: The bank found overbilling and improper hiring of a project official’s family member, concrete evidence that favoritism and weak procurement discipline persisted inside development implementation. IDs: 6B.5; also 6B.4, 5B.5.
- [Analysis: A decade of Jokowi, Indonesia’s democracy icon leaves illiberal legacy, critics say](https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/) — Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-10-14. Claim: Reuters’ end-of-term assessment says Jokowi left behind patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity, which is broad background evidence against a purely professional, evidence-driven service-delivery model. IDs: 6B.5; also 6B.4, 5B.5.

**Search Gap**
Direct, ruler-specific evidence for 6B.5 is thin outside health and social protection. The strongest positives are institutional and sectoral, not a clear cross-government record of Jokowi personally using measurement and transparent correction everywhere. The negatives mostly show incomplete reach, digital divides, and patronage/favoritism rather than a single clean counterexample of anti-data governance.
